results.name: PMF.binomial
results.source_text:
/-- The binomial `PMF`: the probability of observing exactly `i` “heads” in a sequence of `n`
independent coin tosses, each having probability `p` of coming up “heads”. -/
@[deprecated ProbabilityTheory.binomial (since := "2026-04-07")]
def binomial (p : ℝ≥0) (h : p ≤ 1) (n : ℕ) : PMF (Fin (n + 1)) :=
  .ofFintype (fun i =>
      ↑(p ^ (i : ℕ) * (1 - p) ^ ((Fin.last n - i) : ℕ) * (n.choose i : ℕ))) (by
    norm_cast
    convert! (add_pow p (1 - p) n).symm
    · rw [Finset.sum_fin_eq_sum_range]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i hi
      rw [Finset.mem_range] at hi
      rw [dif_pos hi]
    · rw [add_tsub_cancel_of_le (mod_cast h), one_pow])
results.docstring:
The binomial `PMF`: the probability of observing exactly `i` “heads” in a sequence of `n`
independent coin tosses, each having probability `p` of coming up “heads”.

results.name: Ring.choose_neg'
results.source_text:
theorem choose_neg' [NatPowAssoc R] (r : R) (n : ℕ) :
    choose (-r) n = Int.negOnePow n • multichoose r n := by
  rw [choose_neg, multichoose_eq]

results.name: Ring.choose_neg
results.source_text:
theorem choose_neg [NatPowAssoc R] (r : R) (n : ℕ) :
    choose (-r) n = Int.negOnePow n • choose (r + n - 1) n := by
  apply (nsmul_right_inj (Nat.factorial_ne_zero n)).mp
  rw [← descPochhammer_eq_factorial_smul_choose, smul_comm,
    ← descPochhammer_eq_factorial_smul_choose, descPochhammer_smeval_eq_ascPochhammer,
    show (-r - n + 1) = -(r + n - 1) by abel, ascPochhammer_smeval_neg_eq_descPochhammer]

results.name: BinomialRing
results.source_text:
/-- A binomial ring is a ring for which ascending Pochhammer evaluations are uniquely divisible by
suitable factorials. We define this notion as a mixin for additive commutative monoids with natural
number powers, but retain the ring name. We introduce `Ring.multichoose` as the uniquely defined
quotient. -/
class BinomialRing (R : Type*) [AddCommMonoid R] [Pow R ℕ] where
  -- This base class has been demoted to a field, to avoid creating
  -- an expensive global instance.
  [toIsAddTorsionFree : IsAddTorsionFree R]
  /-- A multichoose function, giving the quotient of Pochhammer evaluations by factorials. -/
  multichoose : R → ℕ → R
  /-- The `n`th ascending Pochhammer polynomial evaluated at any element is divisible by `n!` -/
  factorial_nsmul_multichoose (r : R) (n : ℕ) :
    n.factorial • multichoose r n = (ascPochhammer ℕ n).smeval r
results.docstring:
A binomial ring is a ring for which ascending Pochhammer evaluations are uniquely divisible by
suitable factorials. We define this notion as a mixin for additive commutative monoids with natural
number powers, but retain the ring name. We introduce `Ring.multichoose` as the uniquely defined
quotient.

results.name: signedDist
results.source_text:
/--
The signed distance between two points `p` and `q`, in the direction of a reference vector `v`.
It is the size of `q - p` in the direction of `v`.
In the degenerate case `v = 0`, it returns `0`.

TODO: once we have a topology on `P →ᴬ[ℝ] ℝ`, the type should be `P →ᴬ[ℝ] P →ᴬ[ℝ] ℝ`.
-/
noncomputable def signedDist (v : V) : P →ᵃ[ℝ] P →ᴬ[ℝ] ℝ where
  toFun p := (innerSL ℝ (normalize v)).toContinuousAffineMap.comp
    (ContinuousAffineMap.id ℝ P -ᵥ .const ℝ P p)
  linear := {
    toFun w := .const ℝ P ⟪-normalize v, w⟫
    map_add' x y := by ext; simp [inner_add_right]
    map_smul' r x := by ext; simp [inner_smul_right] }
  map_vadd' p v' := by
    ext q
    simp [vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub, inner_sub_right, ← sub_eq_neg_add]
results.docstring:
The signed distance between two points `p` and `q`, in the direction of a reference vector `v`.
It is the size of `q - p` in the direction of `v`.
In the degenerate case `v = 0`, it returns `0`.

TODO: once we have a topology on `P →ᴬ[ℝ] ℝ`, the type should be `P →ᴬ[ℝ] P →ᴬ[ℝ] ℝ`.

results.name: Finset.prod_filter_mul_prod_filter_not
results.source_text:
@[to_additive]
theorem prod_filter_mul_prod_filter_not
    (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] [∀ x, Decidable (¬p x)] (f : ι → M) :
    (∏ x ∈ s with p x, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s with ¬p x, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x := by
  have := Classical.decEq ι
  rw [← prod_union (disjoint_filter_filter_not s s p), filter_union_filter_not_eq]

results.name: Finset.filter
results.source_text:
/-- `Finset.filter p s` is the set of elements of `s` that satisfy `p`.

For example, one can use `s.filter (· ∈ t)` to get the intersection of `s` with `t : Set α`
as a `Finset α` (when a `DecidablePred (· ∈ t)` instance is available). -/
def filter (s : Finset α) : Finset α :=
  ⟨_, s.2.filter p⟩
results.docstring:
`Finset.filter p s` is the set of elements of `s` that satisfy `p`.

For example, one can use `s.filter (· ∈ t)` to get the intersection of `s` with `t : Set α`
as a `Finset α` (when a `DecidablePred (· ∈ t)` instance is available).

results.name: Finset.prod_filter_not_mul_prod_filter
results.source_text:
@[to_additive]
lemma prod_filter_not_mul_prod_filter (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    [∀ x, Decidable (¬p x)] (f : ι → M) :
    (∏ x ∈ s with ¬p x, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s with p x, f x = ∏ x ∈ s, f x := by
  rw [mul_comm, prod_filter_mul_prod_filter_not]

results.name: Finset.prod_filter
results.source_text:
@[to_additive]
theorem prod_filter (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (f : ι → M) :
    ∏ a ∈ s with p a, f a = ∏ a ∈ s, if p a then f a else 1 :=
  calc
    ∏ a ∈ s with p a, f a = ∏ a ∈ s with p a, if p a then f a else 1 :=
      prod_congr rfl fun a h => by rw [if_pos]; simpa using (mem_filter.1 h).2
    _ = ∏ a ∈ s, if p a then f a else 1 := by
      { refine prod_subset (filter_subset _ s) fun x hs h => ?_
        rw [mem_filter, not_and] at h
        exact if_neg (by simpa using h hs) }

results.name: Finset.filter_filter
results.source_text:
theorem filter_filter (s : Finset α) : (s.filter p).filter q = s.filter fun a => p a ∧ q a := by
  grind

results.name: Finset.card_filter
results.source_text:
lemma card_filter (p) [DecidablePred p] (s : Finset ι) :
    #{i ∈ s | p i} = ∑ i ∈ s, ite (p i) 1 0 := by simp [sum_ite]

results.name: Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not
results.source_text:
theorem card_filter_add_card_filter_not
    (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] [∀ x, Decidable (¬p x)] :
    #(s.filter p) + #(s.filter fun a ↦ ¬ p a) = #s := by
  classical
  rw [← card_union_of_disjoint (disjoint_filter_filter_not _ _ _), filter_union_filter_not_eq]

results.name: Finset.card
results.source_text:
/-- `s.card` is the number of elements of `s`, aka its cardinality.

The notation `#s` can be accessed in the `Finset` locale. -/
def card (s : Finset α) : ℕ :=
  Multiset.card s.1
results.docstring:

The notation `#s` can be accessed in the `Finset` locale.

results.name: Mathlib.Meta.delabFinsetFilter
results.source_text:
/-- Delaborator for `Finset.filter`. The `pp.funBinderTypes` option controls whether
to show the domain type when the filter is over `Finset.univ`. -/
@[app_delab Finset.filter] meta def delabFinsetFilter : Delab :=
  whenPPOption getPPNotation do
  let #[_, p, _, t] := (← getExpr).getAppArgs | failure
  guard p.isLambda
  let i ← withNaryArg 1 <| withBindingBodyUnusedName (pure ⟨·⟩)
  let p ← withNaryArg 1 <| withBindingBody i.getId delab
  if t.isAppOfArity ``Finset.univ 2 then
    if ← getPPOption getPPFunBinderTypes then
      let ty ← withNaryArg 0 delab
      `({$i:ident : $ty | $p})
    else
      `({$i:ident | $p})
  -- check if `t` is of the form `s₀ᶜ`, in which case we display `x ∉ s₀` instead
  else if t.isAppOfArity ``Compl.compl 3 then
    let #[_, _, s₀] := t.getAppArgs | failure
    -- if `s₀` is a singleton, we can even use the notation `x ≠ a`
    if s₀.isAppOfArity ``Singleton.singleton 4 then
      let t ← withNaryArg 3 <| withNaryArg 2 <| withNaryArg 3 delab
      `({$i:ident ≠ $t | $p})
    else
      let t ← withNaryArg 3 <| withNaryArg 2 delab
      `({$i:ident ∉ $t | $p})
  else
    let t ← withNaryArg 3 delab
    `({$i:ident ∈ $t | $p})
results.docstring:
Delaborator for `Finset.filter`. The `pp.funBinderTypes` option controls whether
to show the domain type when the filter is over `Finset.univ`.

results.name: Physlib.PiTensorProduct.instAddCommMonoidElim_physlib
results.source_text:
/-- Given two maps `s1` and `s2` whose targets carry an instance of an additive commutative
  monoid, the target of the sum of these two maps also carry an instance thereof. -/
instance : (i : ι1 ⊕ ι2) → AddCommMonoid ((fun i => Sum.elim s1 s2 i) i) := fun i =>
  match i with
  | Sum.inl i => inst1 i
  | Sum.inr i => inst2 i
results.docstring:
Given two maps `s1` and `s2` whose targets carry an instance of an additive commutative
monoid, the target of the sum of these two maps also carry an instance thereof.
